olivia: Quick report — onboarding example for ESM + Cloudflare Workers is failing for folks with strict tsconfigs. Error: "Argument of type '{ token: unknown }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string | { token?: string; refresh?: () => Promise<string> }'".

rene: I hit this too. Minimal repro: in our sdk we have two overloads for makeClient(token) and makeClient({token, refresh}), but ENV.TOKEN is typed as unknown in the worker lib so the object literal doesn't satisfy the overload.

mina: two main fixes: (A) collapse to a single union signature like makeClient(arg: string | { token?: string; refresh?: () => Promise<string> }) — simpler but you lose the separate overload UX; (B) add a final permissive overload like makeClient(arg: Record<string, unknown>): Client; so unknown binds to the fallback.

olivia: I tried (B) in a local branch and the example compiles for module=esnext + moduleResolution=bundler. Editors still show the richer overloads for normal cases.

sam.dev: Agree with (B) as pragmatic. Also add a tiny onboarding snippet showing a safe guard: 
```ts
const raw = ENV.MY_TOKEN; // unknown
const token = typeof raw === 'string' ? raw : String(raw);
makeClient({ token });
```
Avoid `as any` in our docs.

mina: I'll open a small PR: (1) add Record<string, unknown> fallback overload in published d.ts (after strict overloads), (2) update the edge example to use safe guard, (3) add a tsc CI job that runs matrixed tsconfigs (esnext/bundler, es2020/node16, commonjs/node) with --noEmit.

rene: Add a changelog line explaining the fallback overload so repo consumers know it's intentional. Also add a unit test in examples that fails on a real contract violation so fallback doesn't mask actual bugs.

dev-bot: CI job queued: edge-ts-typing-matrix. Ticket created DX-1998.

olivia: thanks — marking example blocked in docs until PR merges. Ping me for review.
